claims.text: The proposed ML-accelerated ensemble-enhanced sampling method will evaluate fusion free energies as accurately as explicit AIMD and TOR-TILD.
The method will retain vibrational entropy, anharmonicity, and electron–vibration coupling.
The method will provide a roughly 60–70% computational speedup.
The target systems include elemental materials, binary alloys, and multicomponent high-entropy alloys in solid and liquid states near melting.
The ML potential will be trained on a limited set of 5–10 ps AIMD trajectories acquired at temperatures within 50 K of the melting temperature.
The trained ML potential will generate extended trajectories using ensemble-enhanced sampling.
Explicit AIMD evaluations will correct the ML trajectory every 0.5–1 ps.
Combining short high-fidelity AIMD trajectories with ensemble-based corrections will minimize error propagation over time.
The ML potential will approximate the ab initio potential-energy landscape sufficiently well to accelerate thermodynamic sampling.
Ensemble-enhanced sampling and periodic AIMD corrections will preserve the essential thermodynamic contributions omitted by less faithful approximations.
The combination of ML sampling and periodic AIMD correction will reduce simulation time relative to both traditional AIMD and TOR-TILD without sacrificing fidelity.
Computational cost will be reduced by approximately 60–70% relative to TOR-TILD.
Free-energy error margins will be comparable to those of explicit AIMD.
Predicted melting temperatures will remain within 5% of full-AIMD predictions.
The proposed method is expected to work for elemental, binary, and multicomponent high-entropy systems within T_m ± 50 K.
Performance at lower temperatures or outside the stated compositional classes remains untested.
ML-potential error propagation may make periodic AIMD correction inadequate for highly complex high-entropy alloys.
